highlights: A shorter Lean 4 proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, based on Levent Alpöge's proof with Claude, is public; it has passed machine checks only.
Anthropic moved its Messages API to Rust with about 70% less CPU per request, and Baidu released ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview with 280B total and 14B active parameters.

items.title: A shorter Lean 4 proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis is published
items.summary: The grh-lean repository holds a Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib. It is a shorter version of Levent Alpöge's proof with Claude, produced with the author's colleagues at Anthropic and Claude: the readable edition is about 300,000 lines, the compact one about 76,000 lines. The README says it has passed machine checks only; no mathematician has read it through and no paper comes with it.

items.title: Anthropic migrates its Messages API from Python to Rust
items.summary: Anthropic says the Rust version uses about 70% less CPU per request and cuts median time to first token by about 20%, shipped without taking the service offline or freezing feature development. The team tested the new version on production traffic, found where it differed and automatically dispatched agents to fix the differences. For teams planning AI-assisted rewrites, the takeaway is that verification, not generation, has become the bottleneck.

items.title: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, a 280B MoE with 14B active
items.summary: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is the first post-trained model built on ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, with a 1M-token context window; mid-training extends the training context length from 128K to 1M tokens, and a DSpark draft head is added for speculative decoding. Baidu calls it an intermediate checkpoint from post-training. Architecture and tokenizer match the Base model, so existing tooling carries over.

evidence.quote: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is the first post-trained model built on ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base , which we released earlier. It is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 280B total parameters, 14B of them active per token , and a 1M-token context window .
mid-training also extends the training context length from 128K to 1M tokens.

items.title: LlamaIndex releases OCRia-1 and the CPU pipeline OCRia-nano-1 for document parsing
items.summary: OCRia-1 is a 4B vision-language model that starts from Qwen3.5-4B and writes a page image as Markdown with tables in HTML, scoring 85.24 on ParseBench 2. OCRia-nano-1 is an 8.1M-parameter CPU pipeline distilled from it that runs inside LiteParse, scoring 59.2 on ParseBench-2 at 27.8 pages per second on 16 vCPUs. OCRia-1 is free for commercial use only for organizations under $2M in annual revenue and under $2M in total funding.

items.title: KRAFTON publishes Raon-1 mini, a 30B-A4B MoE under Apache 2.0
items.summary: Following the preview, KRAFTON AI released Raon-1 mini, a 30B-A4B Mixture-of-Experts model trained from scratch, under the Apache 2.0 license, with native support for 262,144 tokens of context. It was trained on Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French and Thai, and KRAFTON reports 96.7 on AIME 2026 and 86.0 on GPQA Diamond. It is an option for a commercially usable mid-size open model with strong Korean.

items.title: Hugging Face uses a coding agent to speed up Inkling 2 Mini decode by 40%
items.summary: Given the inference-optimisation skill, the hf CLI and Hugging Face Jobs, a coding agent tuned serving on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96 GB for an afternoon: single-user decode went from 136 to 190.6 tok/s, and 8-user throughput from ~570 to 716 tok/s, using vLLM nightly with DSpark speculative decoding. Published serving recipes target sm100, so this fills a gap for sm120 cards, and all logs and scripts are public.

items.title: RLVB rewards agents for answering only when the evidence is sufficient
items.summary: During training the simulator computes the exact posterior over the answer, so RLVB rewards further steps while several answers remain possible and commitment once the evidence is enough, with no judge, critic or reward model. It improves the base model in all nine settings by 17.1% on average and beats PPO with an LLM-judge process reward by 9.3% while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours. It offers a process signal for agent training that does not depend on an LLM judge.

evidence.quote: RLVB improves the base model in all nine settings, by 17.1% on average.
RLVB also outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours.

items.title: NightWatch adds a 0.8B watcher to keep computer-use agents in sync with the screen
items.summary: NightWatch is a plug-and-play framework that pairs a CUA with NightWatch-0.8B for streaming monitoring of the interface, without changing the agent's model, prompt or action space. On OSWorld it reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% with task success on par, and raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2%. It can be bolted onto existing agents.

evidence.quote: a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space.

items.title: LoomFormer lets attention heads rewire their circuits at every token
items.summary: Loom attention interweaves a head's vertical attention over earlier heads' outputs with ordinary attention over tokens, using a per-token matrix memory as a second residual stream. The authors report LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute; on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. It is an architecture change worth watching.

items.title: Qwen-Image-HD generates 4K images tile by tile
items.summary: Qwen-Image-HD adapts Qwen-Image 2.0 to high-resolution synthesis with local training and blockwise autoregressive generation: each 1K-scale tile is conditioned on upper and left neighbors and a compressed thumbnail. On Qwen-Image-Bench at 4K it beats direct 4K generation with FLUX-3-Image-Klein, with lower training compute than full-image 4K fine-tuning. A Wavefront-AutoRegressive schedule generates anti-diagonal tiles concurrently across GPUs to cut latency.

evidence.quote: On Qwen-Image-Bench at 4K, Qwen-Image-HD achieves stronger overall evaluation performance than direct 4K generation with FLUX-3-Image-Klein.

items.title: Google open-sources a framework testing how assistants reason through users' accounts
items.summary: Applied to 12 LLMs, the simulation-based framework shows models are significantly more accurate as observers than as assistants hearing the user's account; the framework and over 20K examples are open source.

items.title: SpecEngineeringBench: coding agents write passing tests but expose few defects
items.summary: Across 100 instances from 78 Python repositories, seven frontier coding agents reach a 91.47% Head Pass Rate but only a 26.36% Fail-to-Pass Rate.

items.title: ACAP runs one robot as a team of asynchronous coding agents
items.summary: A hyper-agent assigns tasks and coordinates dependencies; across 72 real-world rollouts ACAP cuts task-balanced time cost by 28.2% versus a single-agent policy.
